alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Watchdogs deactivated
alarms.long_description: EGRCU watchdog disabled.
alarms.cause: Orange DIP-switch is set to 'Off'.
alarms.effect: No effect on engine performance. The EGRCU Controller may respond incorrectly to any software and hardware failures.
alarms.suggested_action: Set orange DIP-switch to 'On'.

alarms.id: EGRCU-badBaud, EGRI1-badBaud, EGRI2-badBaud, EGRI3-badBaud, SCRCU-badBaud, SCRI1-badBaud, SCRI2-badBaud
alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Non standard baud rate
alarms.long_description: Service terminal baud rate is not 9600 Bd.
alarms.cause: Non-standard baud rate selected.
alarms.effect: No, or unreadable output to service terminal.
alarms.suggested_action: When convenient: Reset blue DIP switch and reboot EGRCU Controller.

alarms.id: EGRCU-SInvParm, EGRI1-SInvParm, EGRI2-SInvParm, EGRI3-SInvParm, SCRCU-SInvParm, SCRI1-SInvParm, SCRI2-SInvParm
alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid parameters
alarms.long_description: The EGRCU Controller holds invalid parameters. The EGRCU Controller cannot start its application without the correct parameters.
alarms.cause: The alarm is caused from the EGRCU Controller automatically loads the wrong parameter set after a replacement of the EGRCU Controller.
alarms.effect: The behaviour of the application in the EGRCU Controller is not correct. The precise effect of this situation is unknown and care should be taken.
alarms.suggested_action: If the involved EGRCU Controller just have been replaced, wait for the automatic preparation to complete. If this takes more than 10 minutes, the LED colour signalling for fault indication should be inspected. If this proves unhelpful, reset the EGRCU Controller unit. If it still does not help, contact MAN-ES.

alarms.id: EGRCU-SInvSw, EGRI1-SInvSw, EGRI2-SInvSw, EGRI3-SInvSw, SCRCU-SInvSw, SCRI1-SInvSw, SCRI2-SInvSw
alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid software
alarms.long_description: EGRCU Controller is running an incorrect application.
alarms.cause: MOP(s) not available during EGRCU Controller power up.
alarms.effect:
Reduced system performance.

NOTE
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise!
alarms.suggested_action: Switch off EGRCU Controller immediately.\nWhen MOP is available: Restart EGRCU Controller.

alarms.id: EGRCU-SIPF, EGRI1-SIPF, EGRI2-SIPF, EGRI3-SIPF, SCRCU-SIPF, SCRI1-SIPF, SCRI2-SIPF
alarms.data_tree_path: *->System->Invalid Parameter Flash
alarms.long_description: Parameter flash failure.
alarms.cause: The CRC check when reading the parameters from flash failed.
alarms.effect: Parameters from flash cannot be used.
alarms.suggested_action: Write a new parameter set to flash. If the problem persists, the unit may be defective.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->ID Key corrupt
alarms.long_description: EGRCU cannot read ID-key data.
alarms.cause:
- ID-key is not plugged in.
- ID-key data is corrupted.
- ID-key hardware failure.
- MPC failure.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect on engine performance.\nThe MPC may not function correctly after a restart.
alarms.suggested_action:
If this alarm is active for more than 5 minutes, check that the ID-key is plugged in correctly.

If the problem persists replace, one at a time:
- ID-key (see instruction manual for configuration instructions).
- MPC.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Battery Level Low
alarms.long_description: EGRCU battery is low.
alarms.cause: Battery worn out.
alarms.effect: If MPC remains switched on: No effect.\n\nIf MPC is switched off or power is lost: MPC will lose its time settings.
alarms.suggested_action: Replace battery when convenient.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Slave failure
alarms.long_description: ERCS - ME ECS communication failure.
alarms.cause:
- Cable failure.
- ACU1 failure.
- EGRCU Modbus failure.
- Commissioning error.
alarms.effect: ERCS - ME ECS communication lost. EGR operation is not possible.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check connection between ME ECS and ERCS (ACU-1 J68 and EGRCU J68).
- Check end resistors (120 Ohm).
- Check ME ECS.
If ME ECS and cabling is OK: Replace EGRCU.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Interface Vers. Number Alarm
alarms.long_description: The version number ensures that data on the Modbus line is agreed on by the Modbus Master and Slave systems.
alarms.cause: The interface version numbers on the Modbus Master and Slave are different.
alarms.effect: All data on the Modbus line is invalidated, until the Interface Version Number on Master and Slave side match.
alarms.suggested_action: - Contact MAN Diesel to retrieve the Interface Version Number for the specific plant.\n- Check that the Interface Version Number for the specific plant is correct on the Master and Slave side.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Modbus Interface->Modbus Version->Modbus Configuration Number Alarm
alarms.long_description: The configuration numbers on the Modbus Master and Slave systems must be the same.
alarms.cause: The configuration numbers on the Modbus Master and Slave are different.
alarms.effect: No effect.
alarms.suggested_action: The configuration number should be set to 0 on both the Master and Slave side.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->System->Modbus Interface->EGR Interface->Modbus Line Alive failure
alarms.long_description: Communication failure between Modbus Master and Slave (ACU1 and EGRCU).
alarms.cause:
- Cable failure.
- Commissioning error.
- Noise on the Modbus Line.
- MPC failure.
alarms.effect: - All data on the Modbus line is invalidated.\n- Control and Status values between the Master and Slave will not be available.
alarms.suggested_action: Check cabling.\n- Check that MPC are running in Normal Mode.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The EGRCU electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more ERCS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The EGRCU electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced.
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->IO Terminals->Ch20,1618-1,EGR Blower 1 Speed FB->Suprv. Ch20,1618-1,EGR Blower 1 Spe
alarms.long_description: The signal from the sensor (EGR Blower 1 speed) connected to EGRCU channel 20 is out of range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor.
- Sensor failure.
- Incorrect Sensor Calibration.
- Missing sensor power supply.
- MPC input failure.
alarms.effect: - EGR system is stopped.\n- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP Alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Try to invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.
If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Gas Supervision->O2 Sensor Supervision (SUC)->O2 Sensor1, deviation suprv.
alarms.long_description: O2 sensor is deviating from other O2 sensors.
alarms.cause: - O2 sensor is deviating and calibration is needed.\n- O2 sensor failure.\n- Too low gas flow through O2 sensor.
alarms.effect: O2 sensor is deviating from other O2 sensors. The sensor is excluded from combined measurement until the problem has been fixed.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Sufficient flow to the O2 sensor (flowmeter in SUC). If the flow is too low check/clean orifice for this sensor.
- O2 sensor: Calibrate O2 sensor via the MOP screen (MOP -> Auxiliaries -> EGR -> Calibrate O2 Sensors. Chief Level access is required).
- If one-point calibration from MOP is not sufficient then make two-point calibration directly on the O2-transmitter.
- If two-point calibration is not sufficient, replace the O2 sensor.
- If a sensor replacement is not possible, remove the ready signal for the sensor, EGRCU -> Ch42.
- Check cabling.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->pH Supervision->Both pH Sensors Failing Suprv.->Both pH Sensors Failing
alarms.long_description: The signals from both pH sensors are out of range. Each sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor.
- Sensor failure.
- Incorrect Sensor Calibration.
- Missing sensor power supply.
- MPC input failure.
alarms.effect: - EGR system is stopped.\n- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check the pH-sensor manual for trouble-shooting.
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to invalidate the signal on the EGRCU Controller. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->pH Supervision->pH Deviation Supervision->pH Deviating
alarms.long_description: Process Water pH measurements deviating.
alarms.cause:
- Malfunction of one or both pH sensors.
- Cabling.
- Incorrect sensor calibration.
- Dry sensor.
alarms.effect: EGR water pH control performance might degrade
alarms.suggested_action:
Check cabling to the sensors.

Check the pH-level of the water by other pH-measuring equipment - in order to determine which pH-sensor is measuring incorrectly.
- Short term: Invalidate the input from the faulty pH-sensor - or unplug the signal at the EGRCU Controller. When the signal is out of range or invalidated ERCS will disregard the input and EGR-control can continue with only one pH-sensor.
-Long term: Stop EGR and dismount the faulty pH-sensor for calibration and trouble-shooting. Check the pH-sensor manual for further trouble-shooting.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->WTS Supervision->WTS running deviation supervision->WTS running deviation
alarms.long_description: ERCS does not receive matching running signal from EGR Water Treatment System (WTS) when run command is sent, within the defined time.
alarms.cause: - Malfunction in WTS.\n- Broken cable to WTS.
alarms.effect:
It is possible to continue EGR operation by accepting to run EGR without WTS before timeout (ERCS MOP => Auxiliaries => EGR => EGR Water => Accept to Run EGR without Water Treatment System).

In case of EGR operation without WTS has been accepted:
- EGR system will continue running without WTS.
- EGR system can be started while the alarm is present.
- Increased risk of clogging the EGR pre-spray, EGR cooler and pump pre-filter (In case of clogging ERCS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).
- Increasing water level in WTS buffer tank (In case of too high level ERCS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).

In case of EGR operation without WTS has not been accepted before timeout:
- EGR system is stopped.
- EGR system cannot start while the alarm is present.
alarms.suggested_action: Check:\n- WTS operating panel. When the problem has been identified remember to acknowledge all alarms on the local WTS operating panel.\n- Cabling to WTS.

In case of EGR operation without WTS has not been accepted before timeout:

alarms.effect:
Note: With this alarm condition it is NOT possible to continue EGR operation by accepting to run EGR without WTS.

alarms.suggested_action:
When the problem has been identified remember to acknowledge all alarms on the local WTS operating panel.

Check:

- Check water level in buffer tank.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Water Supervision->WTS Supervision->Run EGR without WTS accepted

alarms.cause: Activated button (ERCS MOP => Auxiliaries => EGR => EGR Water => Accept to Run EGR without Water Treatment System).
alarms.effect:
- During WTS failure the EGR system continues to run without WTS and ERCS continues to send start WTS command.
- EGR system can be started while WTS error alarm is present.
- Increased risk of sensor failure (WMC switches, dp-PWRT level and low level switch in PWRT tank).
- Increased risk of clogging the EGR pre-spray, EGR cooler and pump pre-filter (In case of clogging ERCS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).
- Increasing water level in WTS buffer tank (In case of too high level ERCS will raise an alarm and stop EGR).
alarms.suggested_action: If no WTS failure: Deactivate button (ERCS MOP => Auxiliaries => EGR => EGR Water => Accept to Run EGR without Water Treatment System).

alarms.long_description: EGR stop failure supervision is disabled.

alarms.effect: Failures that might occur will not be detected and reported.
alarms.suggested_action: Set parameter to enable supervision.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Supervision->EGR Shut Down Supervision Off
alarms.long_description: EGR shut down failure supervision is disabled.

alarms.suggested_action: Set parameter to enable supervision.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRCU->Plant Control->System Control->Manually Run EGR Water Activated
alarms.long_description: Manually Run EGR Water is activated.

alarms.effect: EGR Water system will be run.
alarms.suggested_action: CAUTION: Only pump, valve or BT water level OK failure will automatically stop EGR Water. The remaining EGR Water failures will only trigger alarms without stopping EGR Water. It is therefore extremely important to be aware of the possible alarms which may occur during EGR Water manual operation.\nWhen finishing EGR Water exercise and/or cleaning:\n- Deactivate Manually Run EGR Water on EGR Water screen.

alarms.effect: EGR system cannot switch to EGR Mode Auto.\nIf engine starts, EGR Mode will change to Stop.
alarms.suggested_action: Switch to EGR Mode Stop and then to EGR Mode Auto.

alarms.suggested_action: - Remove cause of failure.\n- Set EGR Mode in Auto on MOP.

alarms.long_description: EGRI1 cannot read ID-key data.
alarms.cause:

- ID-key hardware failure.
- MPC failure.

alarms.suggested_action:

- ID-key (see instruction manual for configuration instructions).
- MPC.

alarms.suggested_action: Replace battery when convenient.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The EGRI1 electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more ERCS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The EGRI1 electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced.
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI1->IO Terminals->Ch22,1687,T-WMC out [degC]->Suprv. Ch22,1687,T-WMC out [degC]
alarms.long_description: The signal from the sensor (Water Mist Catcher out temperature) connected to EGRI1 channel 22 is out of range. The sensor should give a signal between 4 mA to 20 mA.
alarms.cause:
- Failure in the cabling to the sensor.
- Sensor failure.
- Incorrect Sensor Calibration.
- Missing sensor power supply.
- MPC input failure.
alarms.effect: - EGR system is stopped.\n- EGR system cannot start again while the alarm condition is present.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check for fuse alarms on MOP alarm screen. If no fuse alarms then:
- Check cabling to the sensor, according to the installation drawings.
- Check power supply to the sensor (measure voltage between A (negative) and D (positive)). If voltage is OK (18-32 Vdc): Replace sensor.
- Try to invalidate the signal on the MPC that has raised the alarm. This could force the input signal to obtain a different value if this is needed.

If the problem persists: The MPC may be damaged and must be replaced.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI3->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The EGRI3 electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more ERCS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: EGRI3->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Supervision->Too low ECS Insulation level
alarms.long_description: The EGRI3 electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced.
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->IO Terminals->ECS Insulation Level Superv. [kOhm]->ECS Insulation level below normal
alarms.long_description: The SCRCU electric insulation level is below normal service value.
alarms.cause: One or more ERCS components have increased electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.

alarms.long_description: The SCRCU electric insulation level is too low.
alarms.cause: One or more ECS components have too high electric leakage to ship's ground.
alarms.effect:
- The system redundancy is reduced.
- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.

Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.cause: - Valve position sensor failure.\n- Valve air supply is insufficient.\n- Control valve failure.
alarms.effect:
If reactor bypass line is fully opened:
- SCR will be disengaged and automatic control is disabled until the fault has been corrected.

If reactor bypass line is not fully opened:
- SCR shut down, all valves in the SCR system are ordered to fail safe position to ensure air flow through engine.
- Automatic control will not be possible until fault has been corrected.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Valve position sensor.
- Air supply to the valve.
- Control valve.
- That the valve is able to move freely .

alarms.synopsis: dp SCR Too High For Running SCR
alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->HP SCR supervision->dp SCR supervision->dp SCR too high supervision->dp SCR Too High For Running SCR
alarms.long_description: Pressure difference over SCR line is too high for SCR to continue running.
alarms.cause: - Clogging of SCR reactor.\n- dp sensor failure.\n- SCR flow is restricted due to broken parts in the flow path.
alarms.effect: Automatic control will not be possible until the fault has been corrected.
alarms.suggested_action: - Check dp sensor.\n- Make a visual inspection of the SCR reactor, SCR flow path and SCR valves.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->HP SCR supervision->dp SCR supervision->dp SCR too high supervision->dp SCR Too High
alarms.long_description: Pressure difference over SCR line is too high.
alarms.cause: - Clogging of SCR reactor.\n- dp sensor failure.\n- SCR flow is restricted due to broken parts in the flow path.
alarms.effect: If pressure difference over the SCR system is too high, the engine performance is reduced during SCR operation.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Check dp sensor.
- Check in EMS that dp SCR has increased to the current too high level continuously, i.e. without any sudden jumps in the dp SCR value.

If the dp SCR value has increased continuously, load up the engine slowly to a high load, while manually monitoring the pressure measurements in the SCR line closely. This is done in order to regenerate the catalyst elements.

If the dp SCR value has increased by a sudden jump, check the status of the SCR reactor flow path.

1- dp RTV sensor failure.
2- Air leakage.
3- Venting not running.
4- Venting system failure - no air
alarms.effect:
No immediate effect.
Long term effects of running continuously with venting for a long time will either be (from the above causes):
1- high consumption of pressurized air or
2- increased risk of corrosion in the SCR system
alarms.suggested_action: 1- Check dp RTV sensor.\n2- Check venting air flow/supply.\n3- Check for major air leakages in SCR system.

alarms.data_tree_path: SCRCU->Supervision->General supervision->NOx sensor supervision->NOx sensor 1 ready supervision->NOx sensor 1 not ready
alarms.long_description: NOx sensor 1 not ready
alarms.cause:
- NOx sensor failure.
- NOx sensor has not received NOx sensor ON signal.
 - NOx sensor temperature below Dew Point limit 
- Cable failure.
- SCR Control Sensor Unit failure. Note that PLC must be set in RUN and green light for CAN.
- SCRCU Controller failure.
alarms.effect: While alarm is present, this NOx sensor measurement is disregarded by ERCS. Sensor redundancy is hence reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Restart PLC in SCR Control Sensor Unit NOx cabinet on the circuit breaker Q1. 
 - Check NOx sensor temperature
- Check cabling and proper termination for CANbus.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B3 input DI: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B4 output DO: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check NOx sensor, replace if necessary. Make sure to exchange the sensor specifically mentioned in the alarm message and pay attention to replacing it with the correct sensor as the plugs are different between sensor 1 and 2. When replacing NOx sensors, the main breaker Q1 inside SCR NOx Cabinet should be switched OFF.
- Check SCRCU Controller.

alarms.long_description: NOx/O2 sensor 1 not ready
alarms.cause:
- NOx/O2 sensor failure.
- NOx/O2 sensor has not received NOx/O2 sensor ON signal.
 - NOx/O2 sensor temperature below Dew Point limit 
- Cable failure.
- SCR Control Sensor Unit failure. Note that PLC must be set in RUN and green light for CAN.
- SCRCU Controller failure.
- Note that O2 sensors are an internal part of the NOx sensors.
alarms.effect: While alarm is present, this O2 sensor measurement is disregarded by ERCS. Sensor redundancy is hence reduced.
alarms.suggested_action:
- Restart PLC in SCR Control Sensor Unit NOx cabinet on the circuit breaker Q1. 
 - Check NOx sensor temperature
- Check cabling and proper termination for CANbus.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B3 input DI: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check SCR Control Sensor Unit PLC module B4 output DO: 01. It must have a green light.
- Check NOx sensor, replace if necessary. Make sure to exchange the sensor specifically mentioned in the alarm message and pay attention to replacing it with the correct sensor as the plugs are different between sensor 1 and 2. When replacing NOx sensors, the main breaker Q1 inside SCR NOx Cabinet should be switched OFF.
- Check SCRCU Controller.

alarms.effect: No immediate effect. The alarm can be an indication of beginning deterioration of system components.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.

alarms.effect:

- The system's resistance against electrical noise is reduced.
- Additional insulation faults on opposite polarity can cause blown fuses or short circuits.

NOTE: 
Never ignore this alarm. Safety critical issues may arise.
alarms.suggested_action:
Check:
- Insulation level by observing the display on the insulation monitor.
- Insulation level by observing : Maintenance -> Troubleshooting -> Insulation.
- Insulation level trend in CoCoS-EDS if applicable.
- Individual insulation of ERCS components (sensors, controllers, actuators, cabling) to determine the cause of leakage.
- Refer to ECS trouble shooting guide "test for earth failure in ECS system" for further trouble shooting advise.
